fullDescription:
The standard Krabi four-island day on a longtail, with a morning pickup window that tells you something useful about the trip.

Pickup runs between 08:30 and 09:00 from Krabi Town, Klong Muang, Ao Nam Mao or Ao Nang, which means you reach the islands mid-morning alongside most of the fleet. That is the trade with the morning version: more boats at each stop, but better light for the water and a full afternoon left over afterwards.

The route covers Poda, Chicken Island, Tup and Mor. Thale Waek, the Separated Sea, is the sandbar that links Tup and Mor at low tide and disappears when the water comes back, so whether you walk it depends on the day's tide rather than the operator. Chicken Island is named for the rock at its tip, which only reads as a chicken's head from one angle on the approach.

The longtail is the slower boat and that is deliberate here. Its shallow draught reaches water that speedboats have to anchor away from, and the pace makes the coastline between stops part of the trip rather than something you bounce across.

Lunch is included and eaten on one of the islands.

Pickup from Klong Muang and Ao Nam Mao matters if you are staying outside Ao Nang: many Krabi boat trips only collect from Ao Nang hotels and leave everyone else to make their own way to the pier.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash.

Six hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Morning departure with a full afternoon left after
Poda, Chicken Island, Tup and Mor by longtail
Thale Waek sandbar, walkable only at low tide
Longtail reaches shallows speedboats anchor away from
Pickup from Klong Muang and Ao Nam Mao, not just Ao Nang

fullDescription:
A full eight hours across the four islands, which is the unhurried version of a route most boats rush.

The standard Krabi island trip runs five or six hours and keeps everyone moving. At eight, the stops become long enough to actually swim, dry off and sit down. If your reason for coming to Krabi was the water rather than a checklist, the extra two hours are the difference.

Snorkelling is over the shallows off Chicken Island, where the coral sits close enough to the beach that weak swimmers can see it without going out of their depth. The tidal sandbar between Tup and Mor surfaces as the water drops and links the two islands into a walkable strip, then disappears again, so the timing follows the tide table.

Phra Nang is the stop people remember. The beach sits under an overhanging limestone cliff on the Railay peninsula, with the cave shrine at one end where fishermen leave carved wooden offerings to a spirit they believe keeps them safe at sea. The shrine is still in active use rather than a display, which is worth knowing before you point a camera at it.

Lunch is served beachside rather than on the boat.

Transfers are air-conditioned, which sounds minor until you have done the Krabi coast road in an open songthaew in April.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers air-conditioned hotel transfers, the boat with an English-speaking guide, snorkelling mask and fins, lunch, drinking water, fresh fruit and life jackets.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Eight hours, so stops are long enough to actually swim
Shallow snorkelling off Chicken Island for weak swimmers
Walk the tidal sandbar between Tup and Mor
Phra Nang beach and its working fishermen's shrine
Air-conditioned transfers and beachside lunch

fullDescription:
Both halves of Phang Nga Bay in a small group, with the national park fees already in the price.

Koh Tapu, the limestone needle everyone calls James Bond Island, appeared in The Man with the Golden Gun in 1974 and has been the bay's most photographed rock since. Landing at its base is restricted now because the rock has been eroding, so you view it from the adjacent beach. Koh Hong sits on the Krabi side and holds the lagoon: shallow green water enclosed by limestone walls, entered through a gap that only opens at certain tides.

The small-group format is the reason to take this over a cheaper seat on a big boat. Large Phang Nga trips run 40 or more people, which means queueing at every stop and snorkelling in a crowd; a small group moves faster between sites and spends the saved time in the water.

The two national park entrances, ฿700 per person in total, are included rather than collected at the pier. That is worth doing the arithmetic on: most quotes on this route look cheaper and then take ฿700 off you before you board, so compare the all-in number.

A fish identification guide is provided, which is a small thing that changes snorkelling from looking at fish to knowing what you are looking at.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel drop-off for Ao Nang hotels, both national park fees, insurance, snorkel equipment and the fish ID guide.

Eight hours. If you are staying outside Ao Nang, confirm pickup when booking. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Koh Tapu and Koh Hong in one day
Small group, so less queueing at each stop
฿700 national park fees included, not charged at the pier
Hong lagoon, entered only at certain tides
Fish ID guide provided for snorkelling

fullDescription:
Seven island stops through the afternoon, a barbecue grilled on the sand, and a plankton swim after dark.

Afternoon departures invert the usual Krabi day. Morning boats all arrive together and leave together; going out later means reaching the last stops as the fleet turns for home, so the beaches at the end of this trip are not the beaches the morning boats saw.

Talay Waek, the Separated Sea, is the sandbar that surfaces as the tide drops and links three islands into a walkable strip before disappearing again. An afternoon trip on a falling tide walks out onto sand that was underwater when the morning boats passed over it.

Sunset is taken from the water with the Ao Nang karsts in front of you. Limestone holds colour well after the sun is gone, so the light lasts longer than the clock suggests.

Dinner is a barbecue grilled on the beach rather than reheated on board, which is a meaningful difference on a seven-hour trip.

The plankton swim closes the evening. Bioluminescent dinoflagellates flash when disturbed, so the glow appears around your hands and feet as you move rather than across the surface. It varies honestly night to night: darkest skies near a new moon are best, a full moon erases it, and rough water scatters it. Ask about the moon phase if this is the part you are booking for.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in Ao Nang, the longtail with local crew, an English-speaking guide, beach barbecue dinner with soft drinks, snorkel gear and life jackets.

Seven hours. Bring a towel and dry clothes. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Afternoon route, arriving as the fleet leaves
Walk the Talay Waek sandbar on a falling tide
Sunset over the Ao Nang karsts from the water
Barbecue grilled on the beach, not reheated on board
Plankton swim, best on dark nights near a new moon

fullDescription:
Krabi's inland day: two very different kinds of water, and an ATV ride between them.

The Emerald Pool sits inside Khao Nor Chuchi forest and is spring-fed, which is why the water is that particular clear green and why it stays cool through April when the coast is at its worst. It is a walk in through forest rather than a roadside stop, and the colour changes with the light through the canopy.

The hot spring waterfall is the opposite proposition. Geothermally warmed water runs down a series of smooth limestone bowls at around body temperature, and you sit in them. The rock has been polished by the flow into shapes that hold a person, which is not an accident of a few years.

The ATV section runs on plantation and rainforest tracks with instruction and a helmet provided, so no experience or licence is needed. A short forest boardwalk fills out the day.

The practical case for booking this: **it works in the rain.** From May to October, wind and swell cancel the island boats at short notice, and this is the trip that still runs. Waterfalls are at their strongest in exactly the season that closes the sea. If your island day gets called off, this is the substitute that is arguably better in that weather rather than a consolation.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, air-conditioned transport, an English-speaking guide, the ATV ride with instruction and helmet, Thai lunch, drinking water and insurance.

Seven hours. Bring a towel and shoes you can walk in. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Spring-fed Emerald Pool, cool even in April
Hot spring waterfall in polished limestone bowls
ATV on plantation tracks, no licence needed
Runs in weather that cancels the island boats
Waterfalls at their strongest in the wet season

fullDescription:
Phi Phi in the afternoon, the Krabi four islands at sunset, and plankton after dark, all on one speedboat.

The afternoon timing is the point. Most Phi Phi trips leave Krabi at first light to beat the crowds, which works but means seeing the islands in the busiest window of the middle of the day. This one runs the other way: you reach Maya Bay and Pileh Lagoon as the morning fleet is heading home.

Maya Bay closed entirely from 2018 to 2022 so the reef could recover and reopened under strict rules: boats moor at the back of Phi Phi Leh and visitors walk in through the island, swimming inside the bay is restricted, and daily numbers are capped. Pileh Lagoon is a channel of deep green water walled by cliffs on every side. Viking Cave, with its rock paintings, is viewed from the boat rather than entered.

The return leg takes in the Krabi four islands with sunset from the water, then a barbecue dinner, then the plankton swim. The glow comes from dinoflagellates that flash when the water moves, so it appears around your hands and feet. Dark nights near a new moon show it best; a full moon washes it out entirely.

Eight hours on a speedboat covering this much water is a long day, and speedboats pound in any chop.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, insurance, a lunch box, snacks, mini buffet barbecue dinner, fresh fruit, bottled water and life jackets.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Afternoon Phi Phi, as the morning fleet heads home
Maya Bay under post-2022 rules: walk in, capped numbers
Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave from the water
Krabi four islands at sunset on the way back
Barbecue dinner then a plankton swim after dark
